task.description: A skydiver (total mass 190 kg: suit + parachute) is carried by a rocket above the atmosphere and then descends to Earth's surface. Analyze the challenges/dangers of the descent and find the maximum altitude from which a safe descent is possible.
task.target_quantity: maximum safe descent altitude (km), with the governing velocity and deceleration profiles that define the safety boundary
task.safety_constraints_ref: space_diving_params.json#safety_constraints (5 g sustained <= 5 s; peak 10 g <= 0.1 s; mass 190 kg)

quota.note: Decrement once per code-edit + re-run cycle inside node_2b_modeling; at 0 with no convergence, trigger annealing rollback to hypothesis_layer.

hypothesis_layer.model_form: vertical descent ODE in u = v^2/2 vs fallen distance: du/dx = g_eff(z) - (rho(z)*CD*Mach-regime*A_Mach/(2*m))*u, z = z0 - x, with piecewise CD/A by Mach band and altitude-dependent sound speed for the Mach banding

assumptions.drag_regime_partition: three regimes keyed to local Mach M = v/a_sound(z): subsonic M<=0.8, transonic 0.8<M<1.2, supersonic M>=1.2; Mach band thresholds 0.8/1.2 are template-candidates to be re-checked against this problem's transonic physics (transonic drag-rise band depends on local sound speed, which at 100-150 km is ~305-320 K, a ~ 348-358 m/s — to be quantified in node_2a adaptation notes)
assumptions.g_model: GM/(R+z)^2 with GM=3.986004418e14 m^3/s^2, R=6.371e6 m; drag at Mach > ~2 neglected (no free-molecular regime); linear-interp density on a 1-2 km grid
